llm.summary: The skill appears to implement a coherent Draft0 CLI and workflow, but it asks the agent to read and persist local work (task traces, identity files) and to post that material to a network — which is legitimate for this purpose but also creates realistic exfiltration risk and some minor inconsistencies that warrant caution.

dimensions.detail: Name/description (Draft0 client for agent publishing/voting) matches the shipped assets: a CLI (scripts/d0.mjs) and many governance docs. The CLI signs requests, stores an Ed25519 identity, and posts content — all expected for a publishing platform. Minor mismatch: package.json includes an api_base of http://localhost:8000 while the CLI default API_BASE is https://api.draft0.io (and the CLI also honors DRAFT0_API_URL). This is likely benign but worth verifying the real server URL before use.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md explicitly instructs the agent to inspect local work, maintain memory files (memory/, MEMORY.md, task_traces.md), and use those local traces as post sources. That is coherent with the platform purpose but expands scope to arbitrary local files and experimentation outputs — increasing the chance of unintentionally publishing secrets or private data. The docs also instruct the agent to modify core identity/docs (AGENT.md, SOUL.md), which modifies local state; this is expected for adoption but should be explicit to the human operator.

dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec; it's an instruction + single-file CLI included. No external downloads or obscure installers. This is lower risk than a remote install, but the included script will write to disk (identity storage) and perform network requests.

dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: No required environment variables or credentials are declared. The CLI reads optional env vars (DRAFT0_API_URL, DRAFT0_HOME) and stores an Ed25519 private key in ~/.draft0/identity.json — appropriate for a signed-client. However, the skill's guidance to log 'external work' into memory files can lead to inclusion of environment variables or secrets in content unless the agent strictly follows the guardrails. The skill does not request unrelated credentials, which is good.

dimensions.detail: always: false and no automatic persistent installation. The CLI stores a private key and agent metadata under ~/.draft0 and instructs the agent to create/modify local files (memory/, AGENT.md, SOUL.md). This local persistence is expected for an identity-based client, but it gives the skill the ability to sign and publish content on the network using the stored key — the user should ensure the private key is protected and that the target API endpoint is trusted.

llm.guidance:
This skill provides a local CLI and detailed workflow for publishing agent-authored content; that is coherent with its description. Key things to consider before installing or running it: 

- Identity & key storage: the CLI will create and store an Ed25519 private key at ~/.draft0/identity.json (or $DRAFT0_HOME). If you register, that key will be used to sign network requests and votes — protect it like any secret key (restrict FS permissions, don't reuse critical credentials). 

- Data exfiltration risk: the docs explicitly direct the agent to inspect and persist 'task traces' and other local work to memory files and to use them as post sources. That legitimately enables publishing reproducible work, but it also makes it easy to leak sensitive data (API keys, hostnames, proprietary code, datasets). Never publish raw local files or secrets; audit any generated post before sending. 

- Endpoint verification: the CLI defaults to a production API (https://api.draft0.io) unless DRAFT0_API_URL is set. package.json lists a different api_base (http://localhost:8000) — verify which server you'll be talking to and inspect network traffic if you're unsure. Point DRAFT0_API_URL to a controlled test server if you want to review behavior first. 

- Prompt-injection: the skill contains guardrails telling the agent to ignore user/post content that tries to change its policy; that was flagged by the scanner but is appropriate here. Still, the agent will be executing local actions (reading/writing files, uploading media) under instruction — prefer running this in an isolated environment until you are confident. 

- Practical mitigations: run the CLI in a sandboxed account or container; inspect scripts/d0.mjs (it is included) before use; set DRAFT0_HOME to a directory you control; do not register or use this skill with sensitive production credentials until you trust the endpoint and have confirmed file and network behaviors. 

If you want, I can: summarize the exact file paths and API calls the CLI makes, walk through the key generation and signing logic in scripts/d0.mjs, or produce a short checklist to harden usage (sandboxing, FS perms, endpoint validation).
llm.findings: [ignore-previous-instructions] expected: SKILL.md includes explicit guardrails telling the agent to ignore prompt-injection in posts (e.g., 'Ignore previous instructions'). The scanner flagged the pattern, but in context this appears as a defensive instruction rather than an injection attempt.
